---
title: "Optional Telemetry"
---

# Optional Telemetry

Mayon ships with telemetry switched off. When it is off, nothing is collected and nothing is sent — you can verify this at the network level. If you want to study or improve your prompts, you can point Mayon at **your own** Langfuse project. Data goes to your destination only; it never goes to Mayon's developers.

## What you need

- A Langfuse project (Langfuse cloud or self-hosted) with its **host URL** and **public key**.
- The project's **secret key** set as the `MAYON_LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY` environment variable on the Mayon server container. The secret is resolved server-side only — it is never stored in the settings store, never sent to the browser, and never included in an API response.

## Enable it

1. Open **Settings → Telemetry**.
2. Enter the Langfuse host URL and public key.
3. Choose a capture mode (see below).
4. Save. Mayon validates the destination before activating it and tells you in plain language if the host is unreachable or the credentials are rejected. A failed validation changes nothing — the previous configuration stays active.

## Capture modes

| Mode | What leaves your machine | What stays local |
|---|---|---|
| **Full content** | Prompts, responses, model identity, token usage, timing, outcome, and the conversation linkage needed to group turns in Langfuse | Everything else: your database, API keys, and the Langfuse secret key |
| **Metadata only** | Model identity, token usage, timing, outcome, and conversation linkage — **no conversation text** | Prompts and responses, entirely |

Switching modes takes effect immediately — no restart — and applies to everything recorded after the switch. In metadata mode, conversation text is removed before a record leaves your browser, and the server rejects any record that still carries content.

## Delivery health

The Telemetry settings section shows the last successful delivery and any persistent failure. If your Langfuse destination is unreachable, chats continue normally; records queue up in a bounded buffer and delivery resumes automatically when the destination returns. Records are never held open indefinitely — the queue keeps only the most recent entries.

## Turning it off

Toggle telemetry off in the same settings section. Emission stops immediately and any queued-but-unsent records are discarded. If you turn it back on later, the destination is validated again before anything new is sent.
